title: Injective representatives give the two ordinary site-section models
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites in the common universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1), and let $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be its induced geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Write $L=g^{-1}:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, also for its termwise and exact derived extensions. Use the ordinary bounded-below derived categories, localization $Q$, and cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. For a site object $V$, let $\alpha^V_K:Q\Gamma(V,K)\to R\Gamma(V,QK)$ be the ordinary right-derived comparison unit [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], for a bounded-below complex $K$ on that site. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$, $M\in D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D))$, and $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $\mathcal H^n(M)=0$ for $n<a$. There exist a complex $I$ of injective abelian sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions], with $I^n=0$ for $n<a$, and an isomorphism $\rho:QI\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. For every such pair $(I,\rho)$, $LI$ is zero below $a$, $L\rho:Q(LI)\xrightarrow{\sim}LM$, and $H^p(U,LI^n)=0$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $p>0$. The comparison units give isomorphisms in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$
$$a_{I,\rho}=R\Gamma(u(U),\rho)\circ\alpha^{u(U)}_I:Q\Gamma(u(U),I)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(u(U),M),$$
$$b_{I,\rho}=R\Gamma(U,L\rho)\circ\alpha^U_{LI}:Q\Gamma(U,LI)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(U,LM).$$
These maps commute with chain maps $t:I\to I'$ and isomorphisms $\rho':QI'\cong M'$ for which a coefficient map $f:M\to M'$ satisfies $\rho'\circ Qt=f\circ\rho$: explicitly $R\Gamma(u(U),f)\circ a_{I,\rho}=a_{I',\rho'}\circ Q\Gamma(u(U),t)$ and $R\Gamma(U,Lf)\circ b_{I,\rho}=b_{I',\rho'}\circ Q\Gamma(U,Lt)$.

source.place: Tag 0DD8, lemma-pullback-same-cohomology, first proof sentence: bounded-below injective representative and Leray acyclicity for its inverse image

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ is abelian with enough injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative](1) to $M$ and the specified $a$. This gives $I^n=0$ for $n<a$, injective terms, and $\rho:QI\cong M$. Fix any pair with these properties for the remaining steps.

source.place: Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist (2)-(3), with the cohomological truncation in lemma-cohomology-bounded-below; enough injectives: injectives.tex, Tag 01DP, theorem-sheaves-injectives

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] to $g$ with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$. An abelian sheaf has its unique integer action by repeated addition, so the forgotten functor in that statement is $L$. Hence $L$ is exact and its termwise functor induces the stated functor on $D^+$. Additivity sends zero to zero, giving $(LI)^n=0$ for $n<a$; functoriality sends $\rho$ and its inverse to inverse maps, giving $L\rho:Q(LI)\cong LM$.

For each $n$, apply [lem-trf-site-pullback-injective-evaluation-acyclic] to the injective abelian sheaf $I^n$. Its small-site, continuity and cocontinuity hypotheses are precisely ours, so $H^p(U,LI^n)=0$ for every $p>0$.

Evaluation at either site object is additive and left exact, with enough injectives in its source, by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1)-(2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective](2) to evaluation at $u(U)$ and $I$: $\alpha^{u(U)}_I$ is invertible. Apply [src-right-derived-functor-plus-acyclic-unit] to evaluation at $U$ and $LI$, using the bound from step 2 and the vanishing from step 3: $\alpha^U_{LI}$ is invertible. Composing with the images of $\rho$ and $L\rho$ under the two derived evaluation functors gives exactly the displayed isomorphisms $a_{I,\rho}$ and $b_{I,\rho}$.

source.place: Tag 05TI, lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived, and Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity; units as in the existing PlusHomology theorem

proof.text: The comparison $\alpha$ is a natural transformation by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective](1). For either evaluation functor $v$, its naturality reads $Rv(Qs)\alpha_K=\alpha_{K\prime}Qv(s)$. If $\eta\prime Qs=h\eta$, functoriality gives $Rv(h)Rv(\eta)\alpha_K=Rv(\eta\prime)Rv(Qs)\alpha_K=Rv(\eta\prime)\alpha_{K\prime}Qv(s)$. First take $(v,K,s,\eta,h)=(\Gamma(u(U),-),I,t,\rho,f)$. This is the asserted equation for $a$. Then take $(v,K,s,\eta,h)=(\Gamma(U,-),LI,Lt,L\rho,Lf)$; applying $L$ to the given compatibility supplies $\eta\prime Qs=h\eta$. This gives the asserted equation for $b$.
